evidence: Plin. NH 9.159: rānae pariunt minimās carnēs nigrās, quās gyrīnōs vocant (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Pliny’s word, from Greek γυρῖνος; Lewis & Short defines it as “a young frog not yet fully developed, a tadpole”. It is the only Latin word for the tadpole that we have found. rānunculus, which Lewis & Short also glosses “tadpole”, is a little frog (Cic. Div. 1.15, Lewis & Short; jokingly of the people of Ulubrae, Cic. Fam. 7.18.3), not the swimming larva.

phrases.latin: Spectā gyrīnōs in lacūnā; mox rānae fīent.
phrases.english: Look at the tadpoles in the pond; soon they’ll be frogs.

phrases.latin: rānae pariunt minimās carnēs nigrās, quās gyrīnōs vocant
phrases.english: frogs bring forth tiny black bits of flesh, which they call tadpoles

sources: Lewis & Short: gyrinus · Lewis & Short: ranunculus
